However, this analysis can be inaccurate when applied to low-resolution MR images such as single-phase CT perfusion data due to blurring and reduced detail. A new differentiable deconvolution algorithm has been developed to improve the accuracy of perfusion analysis in such cases by estimating the true concentration of an antidote from noisy observations. When tested on single-phase CT scans from stroke patients, the algorithm provided more accurate estimates of MTT and CBF than traditional methods, enabling more precise identification of ischemic lesions and improvement in clinical decision-making.

Zero-jettiness beam functions, which address collinear emissions from the initial-state hadrons in cross-section calculations, are determined at a next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy for $n$-jet observables in QCD. We have made progress in computing these contributions at a specific perturbative order and, for the first time, determined certain sub-components required for the $n$-jet zero-jettiness distribution at the specified accuracy. These findings enable predictions for specific events, such as $Z$ boson production at the Large Hadron Collider, to be made at a higher accuracy than previously achievable.

This study delves into chordal characteristics of the power graph in finite groups. Specifically, we identify and construct the only two finite nilpotent of class two groups whose power graph is chordal, as well as finite groups where the power graph, contrasting with the domination and order graphs, exhibits chordal properties distinct from their combined graph. Additionally, we define and introduce $k$-domination in power graphs and demonstrate the existence of a finite group where this concept corresponds to the power graph, thus mirroring its domination analogy.

We suggest an innovative training technique, Optimal Condition Training (OCT), tailored for separating a single audio source from a complex mixture, incorporating prior knowledge about the source's characteristics. At its core, OCT minimizes the difference between audio examples generated under optimal and actual conditions, utilizing the source's characteristics as a guide. By doing so, OCT enables a neural network to better distinguish the desired audio signal from surrounding noise. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world audio datasets reveal that OCT surpasses existing methods of source separation with mixed prior knowledge.

New metrics have been proposed to quantify quantum coherence in the context of general quantum measurements, taking into account both individual and collective results. The metrics demonstrate properties analogous to those of classical probability in binary outcomes, and they offer a generalized framework for understanding coherence. The metrics also facilitate a deeper exploration of coherence within specific quantum measurements, and they reveal a way to transform coherent states into incoherent ones through a sequential measurement process.

We have made a groundbreaking discovery of Type C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the low-luminosity state of the black hole X-ray binary H 1743--322. In a series of observations spanning 2007, 2014, 2014, and 2019, we found QPOs with high frequency, low frequency, and broad-line kinetic energy (BEK) frequency in the hard X-ray band. Utilizing the extended tangent slab Comptonization model, we discovered that the QPOs are associated with an accretion flow geometry, which we propose is a thin accretion disk surrounding a truncated accretion flow. This geometry is supported by the existence of QPOs in the 2007, 2014, and 2019 outbursts, which we attribute to the disk's radial and tangential velocities. Furthermore, we found that the QPOs are associated with the disk's inner radius, outer radius, and BEK frequency. In contrast to previous studies, we found that the QPOs in the 2019 outburst were suppressed due to the disk's radial stratification. We also discovered that the QPOs in the 2019 outburst were influenced by the disk's inner radius, which we attribute to the accretion flow's truncation.

A novel electronic governance-based question answering system, named JYULu, has been developed for the Chinese language. This system utilizes a specialized bi-encoder model pre-trained on Chinese multi-document summaries, which effectively captures the nuanced relationships between question contexts and answer candidates. The model has shown exceptional performance on various evaluation metrics and has been fine-tuned using a high-quality dataset derived from real-world applications. JYULu has been deployed as a production-ready system and has been utilized by the Chinese government to address a significant issue related to fake news. Notably, the system's ability to recognize false information is transferable to other domains, making it a versatile tool for addressing multiple e-governance challenges.

The standard model of cosmic evolution indicates that a substantial portion of matter in the universe should be in the form of warm, diffuse gas. Observations of this gas in the present day are only partially successful in accounting for the missing matter. A recent analysis utilizing the EAGLE simulations suggests that future surveys of Lyman-$\alpha$ emission from galaxies at intermediate redshifts may be the key to resolving this enigma. By examining the expected patterns of Lyman-$\alpha$ emission in these galaxies, it is possible to identify regions rich in missing matter. A thorough examination of these patterns reveals that a significant portion of missing matter is concentrated in areas with the highest Lyman-$\alpha$ surface brightness. As a result, future surveys of galaxies with the highest Lyman-$\alpha$ surface brightness are expected to yield a substantial portion of missing matter in the universe.

The problem of identifying all minimal sets that divide a given input graph $G$ into its constituent subgraphs, represents an extension of the optimal vertex cover problem and a generalized version of the optimal edge disconnection problem. Specifically, we focus on finding all leftmost separators, which are defined as subsets of the vertices in $G$, where the removal of these vertices results in a subgraph that is distinct from $G$ and lacks any additional vertex connections. To achieve this, we introduce a novel algorithm that identifies all leftmost separators of a given size $k$, where the size of the separator is defined as the number of vertices it contains. The proposed algorithm operates in a recursive manner, where each step involves the removal of a vertex from the graph and the subsequent identification of all separators in the resulting subgraph. To guarantee the completeness of the recursion, we employ a strategy where the vertices are removed in a specific order based on a predetermined ordering of the vertices, which is achieved through the use of a preprocessing step. To demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm, we conduct an experimental evaluation on both artificial and real-world graphs.

Galactic nuclei, particularly those that lack active galactic nuclei and emission lines, yet have high star formation rates or post-starburst spectra, can exhibit a wide variety of non-AGN transients. We analyzed 12 such events across 7 galaxies with 4 Tidal Disruption Events, 2 Tidal Disruption Events mimicking by Accretion and one Swift J2058.4$-$5842 event, discovered through a search of the SDSS and LBTI survey data. The observed timescales of these transients range from 3 to 489 days and cover a wide range of luminosity levels. The multi-wavelength properties of these transients suggest that some are TDEs, while others are likely novae, supernovae, or supernovae-like events. The TDEs are more common in post-starburst, Balmer-strong galaxies than in quiescent ones, and are often associated with low metal content and low black hole masses. The TDEs are more common in post-starburst, Balmer-strong galaxies than in quiescent ones, and are often associated with low metal content and low black hole masses.

In reconfigurable wireless networks, devices with integrated inferences and software-programmable capabilities are becoming increasingly prevalent, offering vast opportunities for customized network operations that can significantly enhance performance and efficiency. To capitalize on these benefits, there is a need for innovative methods to train decision-making algorithms that can effectively manage network resources to meet diverse application requirements. This paper presents a novel approach to policy learning for optimizing network resource allocation, focusing on wireless access networks where efficient resource management is critical to meet various service-level requirements. To address this challenge, we propose a policy learning framework that integrates actor-critic deep reinforcement learning and machine learning, allowing for the development of sophisticated decision-making algorithms. The proposed approach leverages reinforcement learning to optimize queue management, while also enabling the actor-critic algorithm to determine the most effective policy for resource allocation. The proposed approach is then evaluated using a comprehensive simulation model to verify its efficacy. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach offers a superior QoS for queue management, outperforming conventional methods in terms of average queue lengths and resource efficiency.

Current machine translation post-editing assistance methods are limited, focusing on the effects of individual prediction errors. We introduce a novel method that uses word-level QEs to assess how each prediction mistake impacts the source and propose a new training objective based on the output of an existing machine translation model. By analyzing the relationship between QE and MT model outputs, our method shows that it outperforms existing methods in evaluating the need for correction and identifies the most beneficial correction points, surpassing even state-of-the-art methods.

Researchers have identified a black hole in a distant galaxy with a shadow diameter of approximately 12 microarcseconds, hinting that its event horizon likely has a curved surface rather than a flat one, given the apparent size and nature of the object. To investigate this notion, a study analyzed the gravitational lensing effect and shadow formation resulting from both Kerr black holes and their de Sitter counterparts in free space. The analysis revealed that although the shadows of the two black holes appear identical, their corresponding bending angles differ significantly. To refine the topography of spacetime around the black holes, a study of the shadow's inner structure is proposed, which could be validated by observing the object under polarized light conditions. Assuming a cosmological constant corresponding to our universe's current state, a simulation of spacetime around the black holes produced a gravitational lensing pattern that matches observational data, validating our assumption. Furthermore, a study of the object's shadow under free space conditions yielded a diameter consistent with 12 microarcseconds, and analysis of the bending angles revealed a significant discrepancy with those produced by standard general relativity models. These findings suggest the existence of a significant, previously unaccounted energy source, which could be a sign of a higher, non-empty spacetime.

In relativistic astrophysics, relativistic hydrodynamics serves as a vital tool, used to model a broad range of phenomena from stars and winds to black holes. These equations, which govern the behavior of matter, can be expressed in a variety of coordinate systems, including Cartesian, spherical, and cylindrical coordinates. A recent publication presented a new approach to relativistic hydrodynamics in the context of Cartesian coordinates, which differs from existing formulations found in the literature. This research aims to address several issues raised by the previous authors, which include discrepancies in energy and momentum conservation as well as the nature of force terms, and to provide a more comprehensive examination of the role played by the boundary conditions in determining the behavior of the relativistic hydrodynamic equations.

The analysis of the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ meson decay to a $D^{*}K$ final state, using the CDF detector at the Tevatron, resulted in a dataset consisting of 10/fb of data at an energy of 1.96 TeV. The data revealed a significant excess above background, with a significance of more than five standard deviations, indicating the presence of a new $D^{*}K$ decay mode for at least one of the $D^{*}_{sJ}$ mesons. The excess was found to be consistent with previous observations of the $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ and $D_{s3}(2860)^{e +}$ mesons. The analysis of the $D^{*0}K^+$ decay mode revealed two distinct peaks corresponding to the $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ and $D_{s3}(2860)^{e +}$ mesons. The data provided measurements of their masses, widths, and production fractions. The results were found to be consistent with previous findings, with a notable discrepancy in the $D_{s2}^{\ast}(2573)^+$ production fraction, which was found to be 0.083 \pm 0.012 \pm 0.009, in contrast to the LHCb's measurement of 0.070 \pm 0.014 \pm 0.009.

This study delves into the properties of fractal polynomials on the Sierpi\'nski gasket. Utilizing the Gelfand theorem for a Banach space, we demonstrate that the operator's mean approximation is a compact operator. We then establish the compactness of a composition operator when applied to the space of continuous functions defined on a gasket. Furthermore, we define and explore the properties of a finite-dimensional subspace within the space of fractal polynomials on the gasket. Additionally, we derive some bounds for the growth of fractal polynomials and examine the degree of a polynomial functions in the context of Gárciga-Cuatro's work.

To effectively address visual question generation, it is crucial to strike a balance between creating accurate and coherent questions that accurately reflect the content of an image, as well as producing a diverse range of questions that cover various aspects of the image. Prior research has shown that visual question generation models tend to produce repetitive and uninformative questions, which can be attributed to a lack of image-specific guidance. To address this shortcoming, we propose a novel framework that incorporates multiple strategies to promote more informative and diverse question generation. Specifically, we introduce a strategy that incorporates image regions into question generation, which can be achieved through the use of multi-resolution visual features and a multi-resolution attention mechanism. We also employ a technique that optimizes the generation of questions for both accurate and diverse examples within the training dataset. Through a combination of these strategies, we demonstrate significant improvements in multiple metrics, including question accuracy, diversity, and the ability to capture fine-grained image details. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the effectiveness of our proposed framework, which highlights the importance of multi-resolution visual features in improving question accuracy and the benefits of multi-scale sampling in generating a diverse set of questions.

The transformation of dark matter halos from cusp-like to core-like through hydrostatic instability has been a longstanding issue in the standard cold dark matter theory, with the Fornax galaxy being a prime example. Research on the impact of supernova-driven winds on dark matter profiles has emerged as a potential solution, suggesting that core formation could result from the redistribution of dark matter in the early stages of galaxy evolution. This concept, known as the 'adiabatic feedback' hypothesis, has been proposed as a possible explanation for core formation. This review will examine the theoretical foundation of this hypothesis, its implementation in numerical simulations, and various studies on the effect of supernova-driven feedback on dark matter profiles. A comprehensive analysis of the 'adiabatic feedback' hypothesis, including its potential issues and limitations, will be presented.

We expand existing methods for pre-processing formulas into higher-level logical frameworks.  By considering sets of sub-formulas with specific properties, we can apply the lower-level reasoning techniques used in propositional satisfiability to split a larger problem into more manageable pieces.  This allows us to implement a new tool that can efficiently eliminate certain types of sub-formulas from constraints over higher-level logical systems.  Our implementation shows that this approach can significantly improve performance, sometimes making the tool many times faster and even allowing it to solve complex problems that were previously intractable.  The key to the success of the method lies in the way we organize the sets of sub-formulas; we identify a range of configurations that balance the trade-offs between different types of computational overhead and the benefits of the resulting simplification, and we develop a specific set of rules that allow the tool to efficiently identify the best configuration for each specific problem.  This work marks an important step towards integrating the powerful tools used in propositional satisfiability into higher-level logical frameworks.

In our recent study, we've identified a set of mathematical functions that produce replicator equations exhibiting stable or historical behavior. These findings build on research by Sandholm in the field of evolutionary game theory, where he showed under specific conditions that evolutionary dynamics either converge to historical behavior or exhibit unstable cycles. Sandholm's work was however limited by the requirement that all fitness values be equal, a constraint that we've been able to relax.

Random forest regression models find extensive use in both data analysis and machine learning.  This paper presents a method to derive the asymptotic properties of random forest-based estimation for multiple (one to infinite) continuous response variables.  Our investigation reveals that the forest-based estimator is consistent, and its normal distribution is exhibited, with its covariance matrix defined by the product of two positive definite matrices, where one is dependent on the number of trees and the other is a function of the number of observations.  Our results are validated through various numerical experiments.

This study introduces a novel approach to enhance the distribution grid's efficiency by integrating plug-in electric vehicle charging. A communication network is established among vehicles, the grid operator, and vehicle charging stations, allowing for coordinated charging schedules. However to prevent excessive communication and avoid grid disruptions, the grid operator imposes limitations, prompting us to create a communication-censored extension of the alternating direction method of the multipliers algorithm. This algorithm optimizes vehicle charging schedules, minimizing grid disturbances and unsatisfied vehicle demands. Furthermore, the proposed framework allows for dynamic adjustments of vehicle charging policies, enabling it to operate in a real-time setting. Simulation results confirm the efficacy of the communication-censored algorithm in reducing communication and grid disturbance issues.

Using a computational approach based on the density functional theory within the plane wave pseudopotential method within the Perdew-Burke-Ernerzernal functional, researchers studied structural, elastic, and electronic properties of $SmFeO_3$. This study focused on determining the stability of different structural configurations, including the experimental rhombohedral form and synthetic hexagonal and orthorhombic structures. In comparing the stability of the materials, calculations of the formation enthalpy, phonon dispersion, and elastic constants were performed. In addition, first principles based elastic constants were determined and compared with other reported values in literature. In examining the electronic structure, researchers focused on calculating the density of states and band dispersion, which revealed a metal-insulator transition upon applying external pressure to the $SmFeO_3$ sample. This study found that the $SmFeO_3$ sample in the rhombohedral structure exhibited the lowest stability and lowest formation enthalpy among the examined configurations. In comparison, the $SmFeO_3$ sample in the hexagonal structure showed higher stability and lower formation enthalpy than that in the orthorhombic structure. In examining the electronic structure, researchers found that the $SmFeO_3$ sample in the rhombohedral structure has a metal state, whereas the $SmFeO_3$ sample in the orthorhombic structure has a semiconducting state.

The recent explosion of microbial genomic data presents an opportunity to comprehensively analyze gene composition in relation to distinct cellular processes. In this study, we develop a structured framework for categorizing proteins based on their functions and present a detailed database of 16 distinct bacterial species. Each organism's genome was grouped into 20 defined categories, which were then compared (i) within and between species, and (ii) across species, to identify patterns of variation. Our findings reveal a strong correlation between a bacterial cell's environment and its composition. For instance, cells living in oxygen-poor environments tend to have a higher content of energy-producing proteins. Furthermore, we discovered a strong correlation between a bacterial cell's ability to adapt to different environments and its composition. Lastly, we developed a machine learning algorithm that can accurately predict a bacterial cell's environment based on its protein composition.

A novel data-driven approach to model smart building ventilation systems is presented in this research. A proposed methodology enables the identification and representation of the dynamic behavior of individual components within the ventilation system. Through this method, the system is transformed into a network of interconnected components, allowing for the creation of individual dynamic models for each component. These models, combined with spatial information, are then compiled into a system-wide matrix that captures the dynamic interactions between components. A series of validation tests are conducted on various operational scenarios, including fan and valve configurations, to verify the efficacy of the proposed methodology.

We've analyzed the light-curve and spectral features of supernova (SN) 2017gci, a striking Type I superluminous supernova (SLSN) discovered in the galaxy NGC 3324. By incorporating the anti-trapdoor model into our analysis, we've found that the SN's early light is primarily driven by the interaction between electrons and photons in a thin, rapidly expanding layer of ejecta. This approach has allowed us to determine the SN's central engine mass with greater precision. Our analysis indicates that the SN originated from either a highly stripped binary system or a binary system that experienced a dynamic encounter with a nearby companion. In both scenarios, the SN's progenitor is likely a blue supergiant star that loses its outer layers early in its life cycle.

A comprehensive quantum model of the Stoner-Wohlfarth magnet single domain is developed to account for all possible orientations of the magnetization vector within a 2D plane. A new approach to calculating the magnetostatic energy of single domain magnets is introduced, based on the magnetic dipole. The model's parameters are defined using the demagnetization factor components and its predictions align with existing numerical results in magnetization curve and probability plots. A detailed analysis of the single domain magnetization behavior in various external field conditions is presented, revealing complex patterns in magnetization transitions and oscillations.

The task of parsing sentences into their constituent dependencies is a long-standing problem in Natural Language Processing (NPN) that has seen significant advancements in the field. Despite the numerous methods developed for this purpose, a significant challenge remains due to the inherent ambiguity of natural language. One key advantage of dependency parsing is that it can be used to effectively represent sentence structures, allowing for more accurate modeling of semantic relationships within texts. However, a major obstacle in this area is the lack of efficient and reliable methods for parsing complex sentence sequences that contain multiple embedded clauses, resulting in significant errors when using current top-performing approaches. To address this challenge, we propose a novel method that leverages a graph neural network to analyze the hierarchical structure of dependency trees, allowing it to better understand the context and make more accurate predictions. Our proposed method is trained on a unique combination of visual and linguistic data, specifically by combining a visual language model with a neural parser, in order to effectively capture the hierarchical relationships between the various elements. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach can effectively learn from the hierarchical structure of dependency trees, allowing it to make more accurate predictions on complex sentence sequences.

Attribution map evaluation methods, a type of post-hoc analysis, are gaining traction in the NLP community but have yet to receive similar attention in the computer vision field. To address this, we introduce an evaluation framework for image classification that incorporates metrics from the NLP domain. Our method involves applying NLP metrics to attribute maps of various formats, offering insights into their effectiveness. Furthermore, we examine the impact of different methods on the evaluation by conducting human studies and comparing results with the proposed metrics.

Researchers have proposed an alternate model of wormholes that do not necessitate a straightforward entry and exit strategy. Specifically, a wormhole described by double images is defined by two distinct throat locations with one source light emanating from each throat. This concept is characterized by two key features: a wormhole with no singular internal surface and double visual appearances. This study investigates the linear stability of a wormhole model with uneven reflection patterns and a finite, double-shaded structure, revealing stability under specific conditions, namely when its Schwarzschild radius is greater than or equal to 9/8 times the wormhole's throat radius.

A novel inequality has been established, connecting the entropy of a sequence produced by repeated independent random walks and the largest step size taken from a permutation of those same steps. This relationship holds true for any sequence length and is most surprisingly tight, as it indicates the maximum step size directly correlates with the overall entropy, a relationship that might seem intuitive yet is surprisingly precise given the inherent randomness involved. To prove this, a related inequality was first derived, showing the closeness of permutations' entropy to that of a purely random sequence.

Research on the local structure of planar graph coloring is prevalent in the combinatorial mathematics community. This study focuses on the triangular grid, a 4-critical graph, to explore its trimer cover configurations, also known as 1-trimer colorings. Research by Brinkman and Lin on the triangular grid's trimer cover numbers has led to a substantial dataset, and numerous open questions remain unanswered. This article compiles a list of 20 problems related to the triangular grid's trimer cover configurations and proposes a challenge to obtain complete solutions.

The primary goal of universal domain adaptation is to enable a model trained in a known source domain to effectively operate in an unknown target domain with distinct statistical characteristics. This is particularly challenging because each domain has unique class boundary definitions, and directly transferring the learned knowledge is often counterproductive. To address this, we propose a novel algorithm, called Proto-Domain Adaptation (ProtoDA), which effectively adapts models to new domains by focusing on learning robust prototype and reciprocal point representations. This approach is facilitated by the ProtoDA canonical cone, a framework that facilitates efficient inter-domain data matching. Furthermore, our method is enhanced by the use of prototypes and reciprocal points to produce robust features, and an additional layer is introduced to address the issue of the prototype canonical cone being non-canonical. This novel technique is validated through experiments on various multi-class datasets.

This study introduces a novel machine learning-based approach for accurately determining the three-dimensional structure of vehicles from stereo images, comprising two interconnected tasks: vehicle pose estimation and three-dimensional reconstruction. The proposed system leverages a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) capable of generating vehicle models as geometric priors, alongside a stereo image-based feature extraction method. The approach relies on a two-stage optimization process, where the first stage utilizes the CNN to generate an initial pose estimate set, and the second stage refines the results by iteratively optimizing the pose estimate. The proposed system is evaluated using the KITTI stereo dataset, achieving a 3D reconstruction mean absolute error of 0.16 meters.

Answering open-ended questions relies heavily on an intricate balance between producing an outline of relevant entities and details within a knowledge graph, and filling in these entities with the appropriate relations. Current graph-based approaches typically neglect the importance of creating a well-structured outline of entities and relations. This paper introduces an innovative hierarchical model that creates a query graph by first generating entity mentions and then determining which entities to connect with relationships. A dual-stage training technique is employed to refine the model's performance at both the outline and the filling stages. Experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in answering complex multi-hop questions.

This paper outlines novel algebraic structures comprising polynomial composites and monoid domains. The structures for solving linear equations system are developed within the frameworks of polynomial composites and monoid domains. Validation is achieved through concrete examples.

Entity disambiguation is a crucial task in various applications, including knowledge graph enrichment using unstructured data. One of the significant challenges in this process is determining which concept an entity in a context refers to. This paper explores the entity disambiguation challenge within the context of streaming knowledge graphs, where entities are constantly being added or updated. To resolve this issue, we developed a novel approach that creates a local knowledge graph around each incoming entity and leverages OpenWAT, a hybrid method that combines Word Association Theorem and Watson's rule, to establish relationships. Our approach demonstrates its effectiveness by comparing it to established methods on various datasets and various disambiguation objectives, including linking entities, disambiguation, and classification. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of our approach to address the entity disambiguation challenge in real-time streaming scenarios.

This research investigates the oblique corrections resulting from the MSSM at the level of one loop within the context of the Standard Model. Beyond determining the leading one loop contributions, this study focuses on the oblique corrections linked to scalar supersymmetric particles. Our findings reveal that the dominant scalar masses hold a significant influence over the scalar oblique corrections. Notably, significant adjustments occur when the lightest supersymmetric Higgs boson's mass is low, while the resulting corrections in this case are negligible. Conversely, when the lightest Higgs mass is moderate, the resulting corrections are substantial. Our analysis encompasses a broad scope of supersymmetric parameter space, and we have also compiled numerical data for public access.

We propose an algorithm that generates photorealistic 3D plenoptic representations, such as light fields and multiplex videos, of dynamic scenes from changing camera perspectives. This algorithm combines a scene reconstruction method, including camera pose and 3D scene geometry, with a novel texture reconstruction technique that effectively utilizes dynamic scene context. We also introduce a new loss function to guide the model in capturing the visual appearance of moving objects. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach successfully synthesizes dynamic light fields and multiplex videos of complex scenes with diverse objects and detailed textures from short, dynamically challenging video sequences.

We examine a particular category of stochastic differential equations with a nonlinear damping coefficient. Our model features the form $dX(t) = \beta(t)X(t)dt + \sigma(t)X(t) dW(t)$ in $I\mathbb{R}^d$, where the coefficients $\beta$ and $\sigma$ are allowed to be highly unpredictable, with $\sigma$ being positive. The main objective of this article is to establish precise constraints on the expectation of $X(t)$ under the condition $E[X(0)]<\infty$. The significance of our findings lies in the fact that, in contrast to existing studies, the unpredictability of $\beta$ and $\sigma$ can be unbounded, with $\sigma$ being non-degenerate. The key innovation here is that the nonlinear nature of the damping term can be arbitrary, with no restrictions on its growth.

This research examines a type of random grain model, in which a stochastic process is used to represent the gradient of a function on a line. By analyzing the model, we derive the Burgers equation as a limit and investigate nonlinear functions within the model, deriving a Fokker-Planck system in the process. A specific result, concerning the solution of a function based on the running maximum, is also derived, with the model being applied to estimate extreme water levels, and an analysis of sea level fluctuations to test for sea level rise.

Emerging intelligent radio technologies are expected to transform mobile communication from the current 5G era to that of 6G. 6G networks will rely heavily on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) as a key technology. RISs have gained significant interest from researchers due to their potential to revolutionize wireless communication systems. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of RIS in 6G networks, covering its core functions, applications, and challenges. We first examine the principles behind RIS, its architecture, and key technologies. We then explore the potential uses and benefits of RIS, as well as the hurdles that need to be overcome to implement it. Finally, we conclude by highlighting the future directions for RIS in 6G networks and suggesting potential areas for further research.

A novel approach has been developed to downsize complex multi-agent systems exhibiting unstable stability and diverse equilibrium states, which transition randomly over time. The system consists of autonomous agents influenced by proximity effects and interactions governed by a repulsive reporatory law, capturing the influence of neighboring agents. A system where the movement speed of agents is dependent on the distance between agents can generate such random transitions. The proposed method transforms the system into an autonomous system with continuous probability density functions over the entire phase space, which can be analyzed using standard techniques. The system's stability can be determined by standard stability analysis and its sensitivity to initial conditions can be assessed by calculating its Lyapunov exponent and autocorrelation function. The proposed method can also be applied to other types of multi-agent systems, including those that incorporate external forces.

Deep learning models are shifting towards being executed on non-ASCII hardware to reduce energy and data transfer costs. This involves quantizing neural network weights and activations to hardware-compatible types, such as 8-bit integers. The challenge lies in combining quantization with training to simultaneously minimize accuracy loss and reduce the computational intensity of the network. This paper introduces a training algorithm that alternates between model training and quantization, allowing the model to be refined in conjunction with weight and activation quantization. This is achieved through a novel, low-complexity activation quantization method that minimizes the impact of quantization errors. The proposed training method was tested on a CNN model for object detection and demonstrated improved accuracy compared to a baseline model.

The core-degenerate massive white dwarf binary (CDM) scenario is considered a promising source of sub-luminous Type Ia supernovae with the same progenitor system. In a previous study, it was found that this scenario is consistent with observations of sub-luminous supernovae, but a key challenge lies in explaining the diversity of supernova characteristics within this class. To address this issue, we have conducted a comprehensive investigation into the CDM scenario, including various factors that may influence the observed diversity. Our analysis reveals that the mass of the accreting WD, the mass of the donor, and the presence of a circumbinary disk play significant roles in shaping the observed properties of the supernovae. Specifically, we have identified three distinct scenarios: 1) low-mass and accreting WD systems producing low-luminosity supernovae; 2) intermediate-mass systems exhibiting moderate luminosity supernovae; and 3) high-mass systems displaying high-luminosity supernovae. Furthermore, we have found that the observed characteristics of high-luminosity supernovae within this class are consistent with those of the standard Type Ia supernova class.

In real-world scenarios, data is constantly generated, leading to resource constraints in learning environments. To address this, the concept of anytime learning has been developed. Traditional notions focus on the effect of algorithmic delays on performance loss. However, in real-world learning contexts, initial delays caused by massive data processing must also be taken into consideration. To address this issue, we propose a new definition of anytime learning that incorporates pre-processing delays. We examine the implications of this expanded definition for various machine learning tasks and develop a framework to study its impact, considering both pre-processing and algorithmic delays.

The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound impact on the world's population, causing widespread illness and death. Vaccination against the virus has been a successful strategy in protecting people's health, especially older adults and those with compromised immune systems. However, the process of registering and tracking vaccinations has been a complex and costly endeavor, especially in developing countries. In this article, we propose a novel solution to streamline and improve the vaccination registration and management process, utilizing a blockchain-based system that maintains participants' anonymity, ensures the integrity of the database, and provides efficient and unique registration verification. The proposed solution has been thoroughly evaluated through simulations using real-world data from a renowned hospital in Malaysia, yielding impressive results that demonstrate its effectiveness in optimizing the vaccination registration and tracking process.

Recent studies have demonstrated that traditional machine learning models are
capable of learning the same patterns in data that are considered semantic
concepts by humans. The specific nature of these learned concepts, however,
remains unclear and is a topic of debate. Some argue that these concepts
correspond directly to pre-defined, human-based classes, whereas others suggest
that they represent more complex, nuanced concepts not easily categorized.
To address this issue, we introduce a comprehensive framework that provides
a more in-depth understanding of the relationship between machine learning outputs
and human-based classes. Our approach consists of a set of predictive tasks
that assess various aspects of the learned concept structure, including the
representation of class-specific and class-unrelated concepts, consistency
across different concepts, and the presence of distinct and meaningful
sub-concepts. By evaluating a range of deep neural network models on a set of
standard image classification tasks, we find that these different models exhibit
distinct characteristics, which are often dependent on the level of difficulty
and complexity in the task. Interestingly, our findings suggest that even when
training on the same task, models can produce a wide range of concept
structures, rendering it difficult to definitively conclude whether the learned
concepts are in line with human-based classes. The development of our framework
enables researchers to better understand the nature of these learned concepts and
its relationship to human-based classes and provides a set of guidelines for
designing and evaluating models that align

The presence of localized states in one-dimensional systems exhibiting quantum conductivity is attributed to the breaking of particle-hole symmetry, which can be represented as a localized state in a two-component Fermi gas. The system's localization length is determined by the degree of this symmetry breaking. The underlying mechanism can be analyzed through the loop expansion, an effective field theory that describes the interplay between superconductivity and symmetry breaking at low energies. The loop expansion yields a correction to the localization length, which diverges at a specific energy scale, indicating that higher-order corrections become negligible at large distances from the energy scale. The loop expansion also facilitates the derivation of an energy-independent localization length in the presence of strong interactions, consistent with previous numerical findings.

We have been studying a specific type of wave known as the plasmon in an electron gas that's highly magnetized and existing in two dimensions. This plasmon is formed due to the interaction between the electric field and the spin-rotation of the electrons, which have a specific property of coupling. We found that the interaction between the plasmon and the surrounding electrons causes it to lose energy and suggested a specific method for controlling this energy loss by adjusting the electron spin. We also found that adjusting the magnetic field can influence the rate at which the plasmon loses energy. We have also explored the potential of using this plasmon to create a type of oscillator. We also found that adjusting the magnetic field can allow us to control the frequency of the plasmon oscillator. We found that adjusting the magnetic field can allow us to control the frequency of the plasmon oscillator. We also found that adjusting the magnetic field can allow us to control the Q-factor of the plasmon oscillator. We also found that adjusting the magnetic field can allow us to control the damping rate of the plasmon oscillator.

We examine the conformal structure of non-equilibrium dynamics in a massless conformal scalar field using the In-in formalism, specifically with a class of protocols known as the continuous drive. In the semi-classical approximation, the In-in formalism is equivalent to a conformal transformation of the Euclidean metric followed by an actual transformation of the space-time metric. In the Floquet regime, the dynamics is described by a Schrödinger operator with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that has periodic properties in time. We demonstrate that there are distinct classes of continuous drive protocols, characterized by their symmetry under conformal transformations. One example of such protocols is the so-called Floquet conformal charge class, resulting in a Schrödinger operator with a boundaryless Hamiltonian. Another example is the Floquet conformal mapping class, leading to a Hamiltonian with a boundary. We also investigate the relationship between continuous and discrete drive protocols.

A novel method for combining multimodal data, including fusions like ECG and EEG, utilizes a neural network model. The approach differs from traditional methods by integrating modality data within the network, as opposed to incorporating it as external inputs. The method leverages a custom loss function tailored to the application at hand, and by eliminating the modality data from the network's output, enables the generation of modality-specific features, which can be further integrated into a comprehensive representation. The method effectively enables the combination of multimodal data in a latent space, and can be applied to a range of applications.

A study of decays of the Bs meson into its phi and D0pi pi decay channels allows for precise measurements of several important parameters in the standard model of particle physics. Specifically, researchers have determined the parameters of a decay asymmetry (a specific coefficient related to how particles decay) known as phi_s and a difference between two possible decay processes (DeltaGamma_s) of the Bs meson into different particles. To do this, a detailed analysis of particle collisions occurring at the Large Hadron Collider was performed utilizing data collected over a period of time. By analyzing the patterns of particle decay, the following values were determined for phi_s and DeltaGamma_s with a certain degree of accuracy: phi_s = 0.299 +/- 0.026 +/- 0.017 radians, and DeltaGamma_s = 0.341 +/- 0.027 +/- 0.033 ps^-1. These values are in agreement with previous measurements and predictions made by various theories beyond the standard model of particle physics.

This work investigates the use of graph filters to facilitate distributed optimal control for systems with a structured connection network. A class of problems with a quadratic cost function and state-dependent constraints is addressed, with a constraint relaxation technique used to convert the problem into a distributed optimal control format. A novel filter-based approach is then proposed to solve the relaxed problem, with a subsequent distributed reoptimization scheme removing the relaxation to solve the original problem. Filters are designed to maintain stability and achieve consensus on optimal solutions, with numerical examples demonstrating the efficacy of this new method compared to other distributed and distributed reoptimization approaches.

This study introduces the Multi-sensor Joint Adaptive Birth Sampler (MJABS), an efficient tracking method for labeled objects in a context with limited data. The MJABS approach combines two key components, a joint adaptive birth model that updates object density probabilities and a conditional adaptive birth model that refines population density probabilities. This method also includes the development of various sampling algorithms to efficiently update the joint birth model and conditional birth model. Furthermore, MJABS incorporates a novel method to update the labeled objects' measurements and the associated gating function, utilizing a weighted average method that minimizes the impact of measurement updates on the tracking results.

Linguistic databases such as the World Atlas of Language Structures (WALS) offer a wealth of descriptive data on the world's languages, collected through meticulous fieldwork. However, these datasets are often inaccessible to machine learning systems due to their intricate interconnections and intricate data structure. In an effort to address this challenge, recent years have witnessed a growing interest in using automated methods for extracting and annotating linguistic data. This paper presents the results of the second SIGTYP conference's shared task, which focused on predicting features of the world's languages based on a small number of corresponding languages. In the initial phase, a minimal amount of training data is drawn from a language's WALS entry, and in the subsequent phase, a substantial portion of the available world data is used for training purposes.

This paper offers a comprehensive overview of off-policy evaluation (OPE) in reinforcement learning. This highly relevant topic in RL has gained significant attention in fields like robotics, healthcare, and video games, where accurately assessing agent performance through reward functions is essential. We delve into advanced function approximations, reinforcement learning algorithms, and corresponding off-policy evaluation methods. A clear distinction between policy evaluation and RL is made, and common metrics used to evaluate policies are discussed. A few fundamental RL algorithms are revisited from a policy evaluation standpoint. We then move on to more recent research focusing on estimating value functions and policies in off-policy contexts. A detailed analysis of existing bias-variance tradeoffs and evaluation techniques in OPE is provided. A few advanced methods for evaluating policies are examined, and common challenges hindering OPE research are identified. A comprehensive analysis reveals that off-policy evaluation remains a largely under-researched area, necessitating further investigation and development.

In the biopharmaceutical industry, fermentation processes are crucial to maximizing output and revenue, but their optimal management is complicated by biorefermentation's inherent complexity, limited visibility, and the need for near-real-time decision-making. To address this challenge, this paper develops a probabilistic framework for estimating fermentation yields based on past data, incorporating historical output observations and process monitoring information. By modeling the relationship between predicted and actual outputs, the proposed framework enables biomanufacturers to determine the optimal time to harvest fermentation products, accounting for uncertainty and variability in fermentation dynamics. This framework can be adapted to accommodate various harvesting objectives, such as maximizing output, minimizing risk, or determining an optimal harvest quantity. Furthermore, the proposed method has been demonstrated to outperform alternative approaches in a case study using data from a practical fermentation production line.

For a strongly coupled polaron, a tight binding model describes the discrete momentum space behavior of the system, but a continuous momentum space model provides more accurate energy representation. By leveraging the minimizer of a lower bound for the polaron's energy, calculated within the continuous momentum space, the optimal parabolic upper bound for the energy-momentum relation is established, based on a variational approach and a moment method. The upper bound closely aligns with the lower bound and the lower bound's minimizer, and the resulting minimizer accurately captures the system's behavior and the ground state's discrete properties.

We investigate the boundary dynamics of an $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric gauge theory, specifically the $U(N)_k\times U(N)_f$ theory on a Riemann surface, at a large 't Hooft coupling and large $N$. This gauge theory is dual to a five-dimensional plasma with two separate sectors of magnetized fermions and magnetized bosons. The plasma's behavior is determined by a conformal symmetry, which breaks down when the magnetic fields become too strong. Our analysis focuses on the time it takes for the plasma to reach a force-free regime, under the influence of a magnetic field, using a numerical method to evaluate the time it takes for the two sectors to equilibrate in force-free states.

We examine an all-dielectric structure resembling a series of slits, mimicking a litter of feline tracks. The outcome is a collection of wave-like patterns that exhibit interference and exhibit quantum complementarity. This is the first instance of quantum complementarity appearing in classical electromagnetic phenomena.

This research introduces a novel method for periodic segmentation of convex shapes, enabling the identification of one-cycle, two-cycle, three-cycle, and four-cycle patterns in two-dimensional and three-dimensional geometric frameworks. Building on this, we introduce a non-expansive line concept, utilizing which we derive stricter definitions for one-cycle and two-cycle patterns. Our analysis culminates in the demonstration that in the two-dimensional setting, one-cycle patterns correspond to both non-expansive lines and circular lines, while two-cycle patterns align with the conjunction of all three types of circular lines.

This article examines the connection between the Borsuk number and the Gromov-Hausdorff distance within the context of metric spaces. Specifically, for spaces X and Y, we establish that if one space possesses a higher Borsuk number, their Gromov-Hausdorff distance is at least half of their diameter. Moreover, we derive lower bounds for the Borsuk number in relation to specific geometric properties, such as the length of certain line configurations in these spaces and the angles formed by them.

We examine the periodicity of fourth-order differential operators with variable coefficients in a multi-dimensional space, and find that under certain conditions, their corresponding eigenvalues and eigenvectors exhibit a periodic pattern. To achieve this, we use a mathematical framework that combines a perturbation theory approach with an operator approximation. This allows us to derive a more accurate representation of an operator and its inverse under specific conditions, which in turn enables us to establish a more precise definition of homegeneity for the given differential operator. As a result, we are able to derive a more accurate approximation of the operator's inverse in a finite domain, which then enables us to prove periodicity of the operator's eigenvalues and eigenvectors. This is further demonstrated through numerical simulations.

A crucial component in task-oriented dialogue systems is task classification, and research has shown that using dialogue history is essential for effective classification. Nonetheless, current task classification models largely disregard the dynamic interplay between dialogue history and class labels, potentially leading to suboptimal performance. This study delves into the relationship between class labels and dialogue history across multiple languages, revealing diverse patterns in which class labels emerge from the dialogue history. To leverage these findings, we present a new class-label focused neural network architecture, allowing for the development of multilingual task-oriented dialogue systems that excel in multiple languages. In experiments conducted on six languages, our proposed model outperforms the baseline by 9%, and in a comprehensive evaluation of 10 languages, it surpasses the state-of-the-art model by 16%.

Smt-switch is a freely available, API-compatible SMT solver interface that is compatible with nearly all modern SMT solvers. The API is designed to allow users to combine different SMT solvers in a single application, utilizing the strengths of each individual solver. The API is optimized for both the speed and efficiency of large-scale applications, utilizing the characteristics of C++11 and a large set of SMT operators. Smt-switch is distributed under BSD licenses and is freely accessible on github at <https://github.com/akravchuk/smt-switch>.

The non-hermitian operator corresponding to the Bender-Dunne potential, a well-known model in quasi-exactly solvable systems, is analyzed using a moment method. This approach reveals that the underlying weight function can be identified and that the state-dependent normalization factors depend on the energy levels. The results are validated by comparing the calculated moments with those derived from the exact partition function of the finite space, thereby enabling the determination of the normalization factors. Furthermore, the method is applied to the sextic anharmonic potential, yielding the same normalization factors as previously found in a separate study. The technique's effectiveness is highlighted by its applicability to previously unexplored systems, thereby expanding the range of applicability.

Our research focuses on sensors with limited spatial resolution, where each pixel
only captures a single pixel, and how to use machine learning to overcome the
associated signal loss. We've developed a novel CNN model called the MultiScaleNet,
designed to process multiple levels of pixel values from low-resolution images.
This architecture effectively integrates information from multiple scales without
requiring a large number of parameters, and is highly efficient with computation.
In our experiments, the MultiScaleNet significantly outperformed a baseline CNN
model on a range of tasks including gesture recognition, object detection,
and facial recognition even when using lower-resolution images. This demonstrates
that our architecture can efficiently utilize information from multiple scales and
reduce the gap in accuracy compared to higher-resolution images.

The DART mission's planned impact on Dimorphos in 2022 will generate boulders moving within the asteroid. These boulders, influenced by the asteroid's rotation axis direction, may move in the same direction as the asteroid's secondary component during its orbital phase. This study aims to investigate the secondary component's boulder motion by observing its surface features. To achieve this, we simulated the secondary component's surface by generating a 3D model and applied a numerical model to replicate the asteroid's rotation and boulder motion. The results were compared with the asteroid's surface features to determine their orientation. To verify the accuracy of this method, we applied it to the Didymos twin asteroid, eureka, and analyzed the boulder motion of a simulated impact scenario. The results showed that the boulder motion can be accurately predicted based on the asteroid's rotation axis direction.

This study investigates the formation of a scalar field cloud around a charged Reissner-Nordstrom black hole with a specific charge-to-mass ratio and examines how it behaves under two distinct energy conditions. The results show that for a specific range of charge-to-mass ratios, an unstable part of the cloud disappears, while in all other cases, the cloud's properties remain stable. The research further investigates energy condition violations and finds that only in specific situations all three conditions are violated. Additionally, it derives a general equation for the scalar field's radial profile near the black hole's event horizon and identifies a particular charge-to-mass ratio where a thin layer of the cloud is supported. The study also confirms the applicability of the Reissner-Nordstrom solution in the uncharged case, which aligns with previous studies.

Theoretical research suggests that active neutrinos might have sterile counterparts around the GeV mass scale. This could be achieved through a symmetry known as L_e-L_mu-L_tau, which also predicts the presence of a new Z' particle. In this theoretical framework, the mixing between active and sterile neutrinos is determined by the L_e-L_mu-L_tau symmetry breaking and the mass of the new Z' particle. Our study estimates the minimum required mixing between active and sterile neutrinos to observe sterile neutrino effects in upcoming experiments focused on GeV-scale neutrinos. This could be the key to understanding the long-standing 'anomalous' muon magnetic moment measurement.

Significant advancements in image denoising have been achieved through the application of machine learning, leading to the development of a wide variety of models and algorithms. However, a persistent challenge in this field has been the scarcity of high-quality, fully annotated training datasets necessary to support the evaluation and comparison of new image denoising methods. To address this issue, researchers have been increasingly turning to self-supervised learning, which relies on unlabeled data to train models. Although self-supervised image denoising techniques have been shown to be effective, they have not yet achieved the same level of state-of-the-art performance as supervised methods. To address this problem, we propose a novel, cyclic multi-variate function (CVF-SID) for self-supervised image denoising. This approach involves a cyclic process that first applies a denoising operation, followed by a multi-variate function that estimates the noise level and generates a noise map. This noise map is then used to refine the denoised image through a second denoising operation, and the process is repeated in a cyclic manner. The CVF-SID method has been shown to be effective in a variety of experiments and outperforms several state-of-the-art self-supervised image denoising algorithms in multiple benchmark datasets.

In the context of $k$-sparse recovery, an unknown vector $x$ is drawn from a given distribution, and we examine the average recovery error for specific algorithms - the basis pursuit denoising algorithm and a modified version of the iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm. We compare these algorithms' performance under a noisy measurement process $y = \mathcal{A}x + w$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a linear map representing the sensing matrix. 

For the basis pursuit denoism algorithm, we establish a general noise sensitivity bound that applies to any distribution, revealing the existence of a family of vectors $x$ in $\mathbb{R}^k$ such that the average recovery error is maximized as the noise level approaches $O(n)$ and approaches $O(n/k)$ noise level. 

Furthermore, we demonstrate that the average recovery error for the iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm with a fixed number of iterations and the property that $x_i \leq O(n/k)$ for all $i = 1, 2, \ldots, k$, is maximized when the noise level reaches $\Theta(n)$. 

Our findings indicate that the average recovery error for the iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm and a fixed number of iterations is at a lower bound comparable to that of the basis pursuit denoising algorithm.

Union and intersection types are fundamental components of gradually typed languages, traditionally defined using extension types, resulting in complicated implementation issues. Gradually typed languages have adopted various strategies to simplify these challenges, particularly through the use of intersection constraints, type families, and type operators. This work revisits a 30-year-old problem - efficiently representing union and intersection types - from first-hand experience. Our analysis encompasses the development of a modular, self-contained type system for a polymorphic lambda calculus, incorporating intersection constraints, pattern matching, recursive equations, and explicit subtyping with negative contexts. We have identified three distinct challenges associated with combining these features, thoroughly examining the classic implementation obstacles when incorporating intersection constraints. Furthermore, we have shown that a well-established type system for a calculus with intersection and union types, originally designed for term assignment, is capable of addressing these challenges.

A fundamental principle of motor learning is the end-gain theory, which states that an organism learns to complete a task most efficiently by utilizing knowledge of the intended outcome. In line with this idea, we've developed an exploration method that enables agents to learn from watching demonstrations and incorporating goal-oriented random explorations. By aligning exploration with the goal, we enhance data coverage, especially in end-phase areas, and accelerate learning in models. This method is efficient, requiring minimal information about the video or the specific goal being pursued. A thorough evaluation of our technique is carried out using a variety of metrics, including both qualitative and quantitative assessments.

Classically, particles in an anharmonic potential cannot maintain a constant frequency when observed in separate time frames due to energy leakage, but in quantum mechanics, this frequency still serves as a classical approximation that's been adjusted for effects like zero-point energy. We've derived an expression for this renormalized frequency based on a previous study, and found that it also functions as a heat capacity when a particle is in its thermodynamic equilibrium state. We've also verified that this heat capacity matches what's calculated using a more traditional approach, and then further explored the relationship between the renormalized frequency and the system's temperature, observing how the system's energy shifts affect its behavior over time.

We examine the contribution made by crosscap geometry to the late-time two-point correlators within the context of $1$-dimensional CFTs. Across a wide range of $2D$ conformal field theories, we establish that crosscap contributions to late-time two-point functions exhibit a uniform, $e^{-\mathrm{T}/\tau_e}$ decay rate, where $\tau_e$ is the smallest eigenvalue of the bulk Hamiltonian. This result is independent of the stress tensor deformation and thus represents a universal feature of $2D$ CFTs. We further investigate how this outcome relates to the information paradox, specifically the Young's inequality, through an analysis of the entropy of the Unruh effect in the context of $AdS_3$. Our analysis suggests that the entropy of the Unruh effect is bounded by the crosscap contribution to late-time two-point functions, thereby reinforcing the idea that information is not lost in the black hole interior.

The 2021 Twitter study examines the factors linked to account suspension post-US presidential election 2020. The study leveraged data from 2,097 days, from August 2016 to October 2021, and utilized a time-series regression model. The analysis revealed a positive correlation between the number of suspended accounts and the total number of daily users. Furthermore, the results indicate a positive relationship between account suspensions and the quantity of posts. The study found suspended accounts to exhibit higher interaction rates and a greater use of restricted words. Suspended accounts displayed higher numbers of interactions for specific words related to the election and negative words. The study also found evidence of heightened brand awareness among suspended accounts.

A novel experiment is proposed to investigate electron-hadron scattering at the Large Hadron Collider using the LHeC detector, pushed to its kinetic energy limit of 1 TeV. The concept targets specific measurements of the structure function G_F^e that could lead to notable scientific breakthroughs. To validate the experiment's capabilities, a comprehensive analysis is conducted on the electron structure function, covering a broad range of Bjorken-x from 5*10^-5 to 1. The results show that the theoretical uncertainty is significantly reduced, making the extracted polarized structure function more reliable. The experiment will also provide insights into the gluon polarization, a crucial aspect of the strong force. The proposed analysis serves as a model for the extraction of G_F^e in the LHeC and will help in understanding its structure at low-x values.

Crowdsourced image collections, such as those featuring alien worlds like exoplanets, often contain a high level of uncertainty due to human annotators' subjective judgments and unreliable image quality. As image labeling tasks become increasingly labor-intensive, conventional methods may no longer be effective due to budget constraints. This study proposes a novel approach to address these issues by leveraging uncertain image data. The method combines a sophisticated convolutional neural network with an ensemble of multiple artificial neural networks to accurately detect circumstellar exoplanets within a noisy, crowdsourced dataset. Additionally, it utilizes human annotation information to account for classification uncertainty and applies Bayesian statistics to combine outputs from multiple networks and account for individual differences in human perception. The proposed approach is tested using a realistic, artificially created crowdsourced image dataset with simulated human noise and labeling uncertainty. The results demonstrate that the developed method can effectively detect exoplanets in crowdsourced datasets with high levels of uncertainty and limited training data, outperforming standard techniques in classification accuracy.

In the context of V2X networks, a novel method using a distributed approach has been proposed for vehicle communication with nearby vehicles and infrastructure. This method, known as the Distributed Multiple Access Multiple Relaying Scheme (DMAMS), enhances the overall performance of vehicle communication networks. To optimize the transmission process, a new learning-based approach called the Distributed Environment-Adaptive Network (DEAN) has been introduced. DEAN utilizes the DRL algorithm to learn the optimal policy for each access point's selection, with the ability to adapt to the environment's changing conditions. Simulation results indicate that DEAN outperforms other methods with a 10% gain in throughput compared to fixed MAC schemes, and it also improves by 20% compared to a non-adaptive DRL method.

The past decade has been an extraordinary time for Artificial Intelligence, with significant breakthroughs across a wide range of applications. This year's image of the year was selected from a vast pool of over 30 million images on Twitter, highlighting the immense growth in machine learning's ability to tackle complex tasks. As a result, we are entering an exhilarating era where AI not only excels in well-defined tasks but also begins to uncover patterns in uncharted territories. This shift has sparked a growing interest in adapting AI to address pressing issues in healthcare, climate change, education, and a multitude of other sectors. As our understanding of the world becomes increasingly intertwined with AI, it is crucial to explore the profound implications of this technological advancement on our daily lives, society, and human relationships. As we embark on this transformative journey, it is imperative to consider the far-reaching and often underappreciated consequences of AI, particularly in areas like job displacement, data privacy, and the ethics of AI. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the past decade in AI, highlighting its benefits and drawbacks, as well as suggestions for a responsible and beneficial future.

Feature Toggle Adoption, an indicator of software flexibility, has garnered significant interest, yet its relationship with other software metrics remains unclear. Our research investigates Feature Toggle Adoption as a predictor of software complexity and its impact on issues such as merge conflicts and defects. Our analysis of 1,281 GitHub repositories, spanning 2.43 million commits, reveals a notable connection between FT adoption and commit types, including merge commits, and indicative of larger codebases. Notably, our results suggest a link between FT adoption and fewer merge conflicts, and feature-rich projects tend to have fewer defect-inducing changes, although these findings are subject to certain limitations.

The concept of Lie symmetry plays a pivotal role in developing the Vlasov-Poisson model and determining the underlying symmetries associated with specific solutions, such as steady states and enstrophy. By establishing the existence of these symmetries, the corresponding integrals of motion can be identified, leading to the identification of enstrophy as a integral of motion for the Vlasov-Poisson system. An initial value problem is formulated, and the corresponding Cauchy problem is solved for the steady problem. Furthermore, the long-time behavior of enstrophy is investigated in the context of the steady problem.

Recent advancements in technology have resulted in abundant data in various forms, necessitating efficient analysis and processing. This study focuses on analyzing large datasets of document images and 3D point clouds. Document images, such as cuneiform texts, require the extraction of underlying data for historical research. Traditionally, information was retrieved through labor-intensive transcription. This study proposes a method for utilizing convolutional neural networks to identify and classify individual characters within point clouds. A comprehensive dataset of cuneiform characters was compiled, annotated, and utilized to train a network capable of both classification and automated point cloud segmentation. This technique enables researchers to leverage deep learning for character recognition within point clouds.

Recent research on the discrepancy between the measured and predicted values of the muon magnetic dipole moment's order suggests a possible explanation involving a new, light spin-2 particle. This study investigates the unitarity constraints for this particle, considering specific scenarios of how it interacts with other particles. It is found that a significant portion of parameter space, preferred by the anomaly, is excluded by unitarity requirements, particularly when the particle interacts with the fermions in its standard model, except through the Higgs portal. However, when the particle decouples from the standard model's fermions, it remains a possible candidate to resolve the anomaly.

My research explores how domestic factors, including the likelihood of staying in office, influence a leader's decision to make concessions and choose the crisis initiation format. Leaders who face high risks of being replaced are more likely to use domestic crisis mechanisms over their peers, however this trend is reversed when the likelihood of staying in office is low. Furthermore, I demonstrate that the impact of a leader's desire to stay in office is particularly strong in scenarios where the outcome is uncertain and the result will influence their ability to remain in office. Utilizing a new dataset of intrastate armed conflicts in Syria from 2011-2018, I show that the relationship between the desire to stay in office and the use of domestic crisis mechanisms is consistent with my theoretical findings.

A novel distributed representation of binding to thematic roles has been discovered.
Contrary to previous studies, this finding reveals that both local and sentence-level
context are essential for determining thematic role binding, and that individual
concepts are not solely sufficient. Instead, the connection between a concept and
its corresponding role is only evident when considered within the context of the
entire sentence. Notably, the location of the role in the sentence network plays a
significant role in this process. Using a unique external validation method, this
detection of distributed binding has been confirmed, and the implications of this
discovery are found to be highly specific and cannot be attributed to general
semantic processing processes.

Neutrino telescopes are designed to detect high-energy neutrinos originating from cosmic sources. To identify these sources effectively, the detection system must be highly sensitive to electromagnetic radiation in addition to neutrinos. The advanced underwater telescope facility, ANTARES, has been equipped to monitor the universe through continuous observation of the sky. In this paper, we detail the updated methodology used by ANTARES to respond to multi-messenger alerts and electromagnetic transient events, highlighting its capacity to analyze specific types of transient phenomena, namely fast radio bursts, gamma-ray bursts, gravitational wave events, and gravitational wave transient events associated with pre-existing sources.

Ground-based astronomy's precision and detail has been significantly enhanced thanks to the advancement of high-contrast adaptive optics. This technology allows direct imaging of exoplanets, which would be impossible with traditional space-based equipment. Although it has made substantial progress in the past decade, there are still several factors hindering performance, including distortion caused by atmospheric conditions and telescope mechanics. The impact of these factors is typically studied in the near infrared range. This paper examines the impact of thermal distortion on two high-contrast AO instruments, focusing on the difference it makes in comparison to mechanical distortion. The findings indicate that thermal distortion has a comparable effect to mechanical distortion and even greater in some instances. The thermal distortion can be attributed to temperature variations in the secondary mirror's surface, which can be corrected by adjusting the temperature.

Predicting the lattice dynamics of disordered solids is crucial in various fields, including materials science and biology.  The accurate calculation of phonon modes is contingent on the precision of the potential-energy function and the computational methods employed.  In this study, we utilize the nuclear-coupled-embedding (NCE) framework, which offers a reliable density functional that can effectively describe lattice dynamics across diverse systems.  The resulting embedded density functional is then used to compute phonon modes for various materials with different symmetry properties.  The calculated frequencies show a high degree of agreement with experimental data for systems with high accuracy benchmarks available.  In cases where comparison data is lacking, our predictions are verified by damped harmonic oscillators model.  In addition to these findings, we also investigate the lattice dynamics of a biological system, the DNA double helix, to assess the impact of structural disorder on its calculated phonon modes.

This paper continues from previous research on forward analysis for WSTS presented in 2020, building upon the author's prior work in 2015 and 2017. Utilizing an existing framework for forward analysis, we further develop an algorithm that constructs a Karp-Miller tree, providing a clear path to computing solutions using a value-function approach suitable for non-terminating systems.

The large collection of high-energy gamma-ray data gathered by the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope necessitates the use of advanced tools for in-depth analysis of these data. We are introducing a new approach, fermiML, that leverages machine learning to analyze the Fermi Large Area Telescope data, enabling the differentiation of long-term and short-term gamma-ray emissions from the sky.
